title: Z-Tunnel 1.0 and 2.0: where each question is answered

prose.text: Z-Tunnel is how Client Connector carries traffic to the service in Tunnel mode. The protocol, bypass and rollout detail lives in the Client Connector subjects; this subject routes the cross-product questions.

steps.label: What does each version carry?
steps.text: Z-Tunnel 1.0 is CONNECT-based for proxy-aware or port 80 and 443 traffic, Z-Tunnel 2.0 a DTLS or TLS packet tunnel for all ports and protocols: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.zcc:z-tunnel-1]], [[zia.traffic-forwarding.zcc:z-tunnel-2]], with the selection rules in [[zcc.z-tunnel.versions]].

steps.label: Which network types use which version?
steps.text: The version is set per forwarding profile and the action per network type: [[zcc.forwarding-profiles.internet-actions:four-actions]], [[zcc.z-tunnel.versions:version-select-needs-pf]].

steps.label: Where do bypasses go?
steps.text: Not in the app profile PAC for Z-Tunnel 2.0, but in VPN gateway bypasses and destination exclusions, with domain bypasses through PAC files and the listening proxy: [[zcc.z-tunnel.bypasses]].

steps.label: How is a tenant migrated?
steps.text: The vendor's phased procedures for a new deployment and a migration from 1.0: [[zcc.z-tunnel.deployment]].

steps.label: What happens when Z-Tunnel 2.0 cannot be set up?
steps.text: Transport fallback and the configurable setup failure behavior: [[zcc.z-tunnel.transport]].

prose.label: Why a device is on Z-Tunnel 1.0.
prose.text: A NAT that does not keep one IP per device splits the control and data connections and Z-Tunnel 2.0 falls back: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.zcc:z-tunnel-2-single-ip-nat]]; GRE egress with several IPs or ECMP is one way that happens: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.mixed-deployments:gre-ztunnel2-egress]]. A Z-Tunnel 2.0 profile also sends some web traffic over 1.0 by design: [[zcc.z-tunnel.versions:web-on-1-under-2]]. Whether a device keeps running 1.0 when the policy changed before its client was upgraded is open {{gap:client-version-lag}}.

prose.label: What Z-Tunnel 1.0 leaves out.
prose.text: Z-Tunnel 1.0 carries only proxy-aware or port 80 and 443 traffic: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.zcc:z-tunnel-1]]; QUIC then leaves the device directly: [[zia.saas-apps.quic-conferencing:tunnel1-udp-leaves]]. What happens to the rest of the traffic (other UDP, ICMP, non-web TCP and non-standard ports) is open {{gap:tunnel-1-other-traffic}}.

prose.label: Seeing the version.
prose.text: {{log-field}} Whether Z-Tunnel 2.0 traffic is logged as ZTUNNEL_2_0 is open {{gap:log-value-2}}. The field definitions are in the log types [[zia/web-log]] and [[zia/firewall-log]].

prose.label: GRE sites.
prose.text: Zscaler's guidance is [[zcc.z-tunnel.deployment:gre-guidance]], and the GRE side is [[shared.gre]]. The legacy explanation that double encapsulation inside GRE causes the performance problem is open {{gap:gre-double-encapsulation}}.

prose.label: Business Continuity Cloud.
prose.text: Z-Tunnel 2.0 is not supported in business continuity mode: [[zia.private-service-edge.business-continuity:z-tunnel-2-unsupported]], with the supported methods in [[zia.private-service-edge.business-continuity]].

prose.label: Upstream proxies.
prose.text: Whether Z-Tunnel 1.0 works through an enterprise proxy on the network path is open {{gap:tunnel-1-upstream-proxy}}.

checks.do: Which Z-Tunnel version the traffic actually used, from the ztunnelversion field of the web or firewall log.
Whether the device's egress keeps one public IP for all its connections (no ECMP or several GRE source IPs on the path).
Whether the device runs a Client Connector version that supports Z-Tunnel 2.0.

log-field.statement: The NSS web and firewall log formats both carry `ztunnelversion`, the Z-Tunnel version of Client Connector traffic, with ZTUNNEL_1_0 as the documented example value.

quotes: | %s{ztunnelversion} | The Z-Tunnel version | ZTUNNEL_1_0 | Zscaler Client Connector
| %s{ztunnelversion} | The Z-Tunnel version | ZTUNNEL_1_0 | Zscaler Client Connector

log-value-2.title: The ztunnelversion value for Z-Tunnel 2.0 traffic
log-value-2.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZIA web logs show ztunnelversion as ZTUNNEL_1_0 or ZTUNNEL_2_0. The NSS format tables give only ZTUNNEL_1_0 as an example; no captured source lists the value for Z-Tunnel 2.0.
log-value-2.blocks: telling from logs whether a device fell back from Z-Tunnel 2.0

client-version-lag.title: Devices on an older client after the profile selects Z-Tunnel 2.0
client-version-lag.detail: Unverified legacy statement: tenants that changed the forwarding profile to Z-Tunnel 2.0 before upgrading the Client Connector agent keep running on Z-Tunnel 1.0. The sources say only that Z-Tunnel 2.0 needs a supported Client Connector version; what an unsupported client does with a Z-Tunnel 2.0 profile is not stated.
client-version-lag.blocks: explaining Z-Tunnel 1.0 traffic from devices whose profile selects 2.0

gre-double-encapsulation.title: Why Z-Tunnel 2.0 through GRE degrades performance
gre-double-encapsulation.detail: Unverified legacy statement: double-encapsulating Z-Tunnel 2.0 DTLS or TLS traffic inside a GRE tunnel causes overhead and MTU fragmentation that degrade performance. The vendor says only that the GRE options prevent performance issues; the mechanism is not stated.
gre-double-encapsulation.blocks: explaining Z-Tunnel 2.0 performance at a GRE site with a single egress IP

tunnel-1-upstream-proxy.title: Z-Tunnel 1.0 through an enterprise proxy
tunnel-1-upstream-proxy.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Z-Tunnel 1.0 works in environments where the network enforces HTTP proxy semantics and is compatible with enterprise network-layer proxies. No captured source states it.
tunnel-1-upstream-proxy.blocks: choosing a Z-Tunnel version where an upstream proxy sits on the path

tunnel-1-other-traffic.title: Traffic Z-Tunnel 1.0 does not carry
tunnel-1-other-traffic.detail: Unverified legacy statement: under Z-Tunnel 1.0, UDP, non-web TCP, ICMP and non-standard-port traffic are not forwarded and either go direct or are blocked depending on the local firewall policy. The sources state what Z-Tunnel 1.0 carries and, for QUIC, that it leaves the device directly; no source states the outcome for the other traffic or the role of the local firewall.
tunnel-1-other-traffic.blocks: saying whether non-web traffic from a Z-Tunnel 1.0 device reaches the internet uninspected
